test_title: PYST 41 - SSC CHSL 2025 - General Awareness (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following pair of dynasty - region is correct?

I. Rashtrakuta - Tamil Nadu

Il. Gurjara-Pratihara - Rajasthan
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Statement I: Rashtrakuta - Tamil Nadu** 

• The **Rashtrakutas** were a prominent dynasty in Indian history, ruling from the 8th to 10th century CE.

• They primarily ruled over the Deccan region, with their empire extending across parts of modern-day **Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh**.

• They did not have Tamil Nadu as a significant part of their empire. Hence, *this statement is incorrect.*

• **Statement II: Gurjara-Pratihara - Rajasthan** 

• The **Gurjara-Pratiharas** were a powerful dynasty in northern India, especially during the 8th to 11th centuries.

• They had a stronghold in parts of modern-day **Rajasthan**, along with regions of Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.

• Their capital was initially at **Bhinmal (Rajasthan)**, later shifting to Kanauj, which became a prominent center of their empire. Hence, *this statement is correct.*

• Based on the above, only **Statement II** is correct, making the correct option **Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__

• **Rashtrakutas**: 

• The Rashtrakutas were known for their contributions to art and architecture, notably the **Kailasa Temple at Ellora**, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

• They ruled from their capital at **Manyakheta** (modern-day Malkhed in Karnataka).

• Their empire was known for its tolerance towards different religions, including **Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism**.

• The Rashtrakutas played a significant role in southern India but did not have Tamil Nadu as a major part of their territory.

• **Gurjara-Pratiharas**: 

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas were one of the three major dynasties involved in the tripartite struggle for control over **Kanauj**, alongside the Rashtrakutas and the Palas.

• Their capital, Kanauj, became a prominent political and cultural hub during their reign.

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas are also known for their patronage of art and architecture, including the construction of temples in **Rajasthan** and other regions.

• They played a crucial role in defending India against Arab invasions in the early medieval period.

• **Key Characteristics of Tamil Nadu During the Rashtrakuta Period**: 

• Tamil Nadu during this period was dominated by the **Pallavas** and later the **Cholas**.

• These dynasties were responsible for some of the iconic Dravidian architecture, including the temples at Mahabalipuram and Thanjavur.

• The Rashtrakutas had limited influence in Tamil Nadu, focusing more on the Deccan and central India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Rashtrakutas:** Their empire was at its peak under **Amoghavarsha I**, who was known for his contributions to Kannada literature.

• **Gurjara-Pratiharas:** The dynasty declined after the invasions of the **Turks** and internal conflicts.

• **Tripartite Struggle:** This was a prolonged conflict between the **Rashtrakutas, Gurjara-Pratiharas, and Palas** for control over northern India.

• **Tamil Nadu:** Dominated by the Chola dynasty during the medieval period, which was known for its maritime power and contributions to art and architecture.
